## Hypothesis 1

The perceived morality of infidelity will effect willingness to marry without love.

### Variables and descriptive statistics

- **Perceived Morality (`percMoral`):** Points allocated to the perceived morality. A composite variable of two measures of reported morality relating to infidelity (infmoral_sex and infmoral_emo) on a Likert scale from 1-7. Perceived wrongness of infidelity: mean of infmoral_sex and infmoral_emo; both responses required. Items range from 1=Not at all wrong to 7=Extremely wrong. No reversal; higher scores indicate greater perceived wrongness.

- **Matrimonial Directedness (`Love_would_you_marry_1`):** Reported willingness to marry without love on a scale of 0 to 100. According to the codebook: Willingness to marry without love: 0=Definitely would not, 100=Definitely would.

```{r}
#| label: h1-descriptives
# Count respondents in each group.
table(h1Data$percMoral)
table(h1Data$Love_would_you_marry_1)

#| label: h1-descriptives
# Summarize attractiveness points separately for each group.
by(h1Data$Love_would_you_marry_1, h1Data$percMoral, summary)
```

### Graph

@fig-moralityOfLove shows the reported morals on infidelity by the reported willingness to marry someone without love. The half-violin shows the shape of the distribution and the dots represent individual responses.

```{r}
#| label: fig-moralityOfLove
#| fig-cap: "Inherent Morality of Infidelity's influence on Willingness to Marry"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

###JK: Use your corrected H1 scatterplot in the Quarto report too. ###
# Both H1 variables are continuous. Reuse the scatterplot from your revised visualization script so the report shows their relationship on the original numerical scales.
# The H2 boxplot is appropriate for sex-at-birth groups and dressing time.
###  End of comment ###

h1Rain <- ggplot(data=h1Data,
                aes(x= factor(percMoral),
                    y=Love_would_you_marry_1))+
  labs(x="Morality of Infidelity",
        y="Willingness to Marry without Love",
        title="Inherent Morality of Infidelity's influence on Willingness to marry without love")+
  geom_rain(alpha=.5)

h1Rain
```


## Hypothesis 2

Sex will affect time spent dressing well.

### Variables and descriptive statistics

- **Sex at birth (`Sex_birth`):** A categorical variable with three groups: Male, Female, and Intersex.
- **Time spent dressing well (`Time_A_dress_1`):** Daily time spent dressing well; 0-360 questionnaire with 360 representing 6 hours or more; zero is valid

```{r}
#| label: h2-timeDress
summary(h2Data[,"Time_A_dress_1"])

#data$Sex_birth <- factor(data$Sex_birth, 
#                         levels=c(0,1,2),
#                         labels=c("Male","Female","Intersex"))
```

### Graph

@fig-timeDress shows the relationship between sex at birth and time spent dressing well. The line summarizes the linear trend.

```{r}
#| label: fig-timeDress
#| fig-cap: "Relationship between Sex at Birth and Time Spent Dressing Well"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

h2Box <- ggplot(data=h2Data,
                aes(x=Sex_birth,
                    y=Time_A_dress_1,
                    fill=Sex_birth))+
  geom_boxplot () +
  labs(x="Sex assigned at birth",
        y="Amount of time spent on dressing well",
        title="Time spent dressing well by sex")+
  theme_gray(base_size=8) #changes font size

h2Box
```
